label: PF Backlog 635
title: RCCA: inject review learnings at design/grooming time (not only at Gate 1.5) via a design-guardrails block

brief.problem: Learnings were only written to the correction ledger and shown to the 1.5 reviewer, so the original design/grooming phase did not benefit and 1.5 kept re-discovering the same classes.
brief.what_adds: A design-guardrails block (ledger rules + checklist + recurrence) injected at design/grooming time and in the design prompt.
brief.why: Corrections must shape the design up front, not be re-found in review; that is how review findings shrink over time.

objective: Feed review learnings into the design/grooming phase so 1.5 verifies rather than discovers; keep the ledger/checklist/RAG sources.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/dev/design_guardrails.py --item <ID> emits the generic checklist plus the most relevant CORRECTION-LEDGER rules and recurring review findings for that item.
The design-mode review prompt (architect_review.py run/emit --mode design) includes the same design-guardrails block so the author and reviewer work from the same guidance.
design_guardrails.py --record stores the applied guardrails on the item evidence idempotently, and the design/grooming phase requires running it before writing the design.
Docs (REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE / MODEL-ASSISTED-ENGINEERING) state that learnings are injected at design time; 1.5 only verifies, it does not first-discover.
A test covers relevance selection (a ledger rule matched by item keywords) and idempotent --record behaviour.
in_scope: RCCA: inject review learnings at design/grooming time (not only at Gate 1.5) via a design-guardrails block
approach: RCCA: inject review learnings at design/grooming time (not only at Gate 1.5) via a design-guardrails block
verification: design_guardrails.py injects checklist + relevant CORRECTION-LEDGER rules + recurring findings at design time; design-mode prompt includes it; tests added.
precheck fast PASS (44 gates) + Gate 2.5 clean (0 findings) + pytest; PR #260 merged (0decb70f).

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend core/grooming.py and core/learnings.py to surface review learnings (from design_critic/cross_review review history) as a design-guardrails block during grooming; expose via /api/v1/backlog/grooming/guidelines and enrich item context-review output with prior-gate lessons.
dependency_findings: RELATED BI-PF-1466: enforcement works best once learnings exist at design time
REQUIRES core/learnings.py data populated from prior reviews (assumed existing)
conflict_findings: Low conflict risk: BI-PF-0432 and BI-PF-0389 touch backlog/grooming but different concern (dedup, staleness)
config/grooming-guidelines.json may be concurrently edited - coordinate
duplication_findings: BI-PF-1466 gates enforcement at new->in_progress; this injects learnings earlier (grooming) - complementary, not duplicate
config/review-focus.json and arch-review baselines partially overlap but serve Gate 1.5 checks, not grooming-time guidance
analysis.rationale: Item reuses existing learnings, design_critic and grooming infrastructure to inject review lessons at design time, closing the gap before Gate 1.5 enforcement (BI-PF-1466). Pure extension; no new component needed.
assumptions: Review learnings are persisted/queryable via core/learnings.py
Grooming already renders guidelines from config/grooming-guidelines.json
Design reviews at Gate 1.5 produce reusable BLOCKER/MAJOR patterns
risks: Learnings data may be sparse/noisy early, reducing guardrail value
Guidelines block could bloat grooming output
Mapping reviews to new designs may produce false positives
missing_info: Which review learnings qualify (BLOCKER/MAJOR only vs all)?
Should guardrails be advisory text or structured checklist items?
Retention window for learning injection (per-project vs global)?

context_review.reason: Every field just repeats the title; no concrete change, mechanism, files, or success criteria are specified.

api_impact.reason: process/tooling change: no external API surface (dev scripts + gates + docs).
